content_plan.marinade: One complete marinade centred on a single protein or occasion. Slide 1: hero shot of marinated, deeply coloured, glistening protein on a clean dark or neutral surface — absolutely no text, numbers, or labels anywhere on the image. Slide 2: aesthetic flat-lay of raw ingredients grouped loosely by colour or texture — purely photographic, nothing annotated. Slides 3-4: visual process contrast — protein submerging into the marinade bath, then the vivid colour and sheen transformation after marinating — zero overlaid text or graphics. Final slide: finished plated dish in warm directional light, garnished but not cluttered. ALL ratios, times, substitution tips, and any step-by-step information belong in the caption exclusively.
content_plan.sauce: A versatile sauce, glaze, or dressing built around one central flavour profile. Slide 1: hero shot of finished sauce — glossy, richly coloured, in a small bowl or pooled on a clean surface, absolutely no text or labels on the image. Slide 2: sauce poured or spooned in motion — purely photographic, capturing sheen and viscosity. Slides 3-4: the sauce applied to two visually distinct foods to signal versatility (e.g. over charred chicken AND roasted vegetables) — no text overlays. Final slide: extreme close-up of sauce texture and colour. ALL ratios, quantities, ingredient lists, usage ideas, and save or send prompts belong in the caption only.

caption_strategy: Every caption must open with a strong search-friendly first line that names the dish, marinade, or sauce explicitly (e.g. 'Garlic-miso chicken marinade — 3 ingredients') so it surfaces in keyword search. Follow immediately with the full recipe or ratio in plain text, since all numbers and quantities are forbidden on images. Use a mid-caption soft CTA that triggers a send ('Send this to someone who needs a weeknight dinner upgrade') and close with a save prompt ('Save so you have it when you need it'). Write in a direct, knowledgeable but warm tone — no filler phrases. Keep paragraphs short; use line breaks for readability. Aim for 150-280 characters before the 'more' cut so the hook is fully visible.
hashtag_strategy: Use 3-5 hashtags maximum, placed at the end of the caption after a line break. Prioritise mid-size food-specific tags (100k-2M posts) over giant generic ones: for example #marinaderecipe, #saucegame, #homecookingtips, #weeknightdinner, #foodtechnique. Rotate one hyper-niche tag per post (e.g. #misomarinade, #chimichurrisauce) to capture intent-driven search. Avoid mega-tags like #food or #recipe — they provide no discoverability lift at this account size. Hashtags are a minor lever; keyword density in the caption body matters far more for 2026 Instagram search ranking.
learnings: All 13 posts show near-identical, near-zero engagement across every theme and slot — this is a cold-start signal problem, not a content quality problem. The account has 1 follower and reaches only 1.7-2.2 accounts per post, meaning almost no non-follower distribution yet. Priority actions: (1) Make captions aggressively keyword-rich from the very first line to capture search traffic. (2) Every post needs an explicit send CTA — sends are the #1 growth signal. (3) Hold cadence at 4/week; do not ramp until reach climbs above ~10 per post. (4) Retire technique theme — lowest reach, lowest shareability cues; double down on marinade and sauce.
